articleSummary: Avian influenza A(H5N1) re-emerged since 2020, spreading among wild birds, farms across Europe, Americas, Asia and Oceania, Australia and New Zealand. Human risk remains low; cases are rare and linked to intense contact with infected birds or contaminated environments, with no sustained human-to-human transmission, and cooked poultry is not shown to transmit the virus. Migratory waterfowl are the main reservoirs; farm spread occurs through contact with infected birds, feces, secretions, water, feed, equipment, vehicles, or contaminated materials. In poultry, sudden death is characteristic; other signs include respiratory symptoms, reduced egg production, and swollen, purplish combs or wattles, plus leg hemorrhages. Protocols require isolation, culling, disinfection, and enhanced surveillance, and can trigger import suspensions on poultry products. Brazil detections began in 2023 in wild birds; in May 2025 a farm in Montenegro, Rio Grande do Sul, confirmed H5N1, triggering culling, decontamination, monitoring, and later lifting export restrictions as surveillance stayed clear.

articleSummary: Five brand-new human-infecting tick-borne viruses identified in the last decade include three in China, one in Japan, and one in California. articleSummary: Campylobacter fetus subsp. venerealis (Cfv) causes bovine genital Campylobacteriosis, a venereal disease contributing to reproductive losses in natural-service herds. In Brazil, 44 heifers were allocated to four groups: G1 vaccine A, G2 vaccine B, G3 infected with placebo, G4 negative control. After intravaginal challenge with Cfv, animals were followed for 105 days. Culture of vaginal-cervical mucus showed lower positivity in vaccinated groups (G1 61.81%, G2 45.45%) versus G3 87.27% (p<0.05). Local IgA and systemic IgG responses were detected by ELISA in all challenged groups, with earlier increases in G1/G2. Agglutinating antibodies were observed post-vaccination, strongest in G2 (p=0.0316). qPCR indicated a lower bacterial load in vaccinated cattle during sampling. Conclusion: vaccines yielded significantly earlier clearance of Cfv from the reproductive tract, associated with elevated early humoral responses; vaccines merit field evaluation to assess reproductive performance.
